reading.title: Drift Bottles and the Mapping of Ocean Currents
reading.intro_zh: 这篇拓展阅读讲述真实的海洋学方法——科学家如何用“漂流瓶”追踪洋流，改编自美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA Fisheries）的权威资料，难度提升到 B2+。

source.title: Messages in a Bottle: Ocean Feature Mapping

passage: Long before satellites mapped the seas, oceanographers faced a stubborn problem: the currents that steer marine life and disperse fish larvae are invisible, and tracking them across thousands of square miles by ship alone was impractical. Their ingenious, low-cost solution was the drift bottle. A sealed bottle containing a numbered card was released at a known position, then carried wherever the surface water flowed. Each one was, in effect, a slow data probe disguised as a message in a bottle.

The method depended on ordinary people. Whoever recovered a bottle was asked to note the date and location and mail the card back. By comparing the release point with the recovery point, scientists could reconstruct the direction and approximate speed of a current. The effort grew remarkable in scale: American researchers released more than seventy thousand drift bottles and seabed drifters during the 1960s programme, some launched from aircraft sweeping along the Atlantic shelf.

The technique was charmingly imprecise. A bottle revealed only where it began and where it ended, never the winding route between, and a single card might surface decades later, far from anywhere predictable. Today, GPS-equipped drifting buoys transmit their coordinates continuously by satellite, yielding the detailed, real-time picture that scattered bottles never could. Yet the underlying logic endures: to chart something unseen, you scatter many markers and patiently gather what drifts home.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The romantic appeal of sending personal messages across the ocean.
How modern satellites have made all ocean research unnecessary.
How scientists used drift bottles to study invisible ocean currents.
The danger that floating glass bottles pose to marine animals.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕科学家如何利用漂流瓶来研究看不见的洋流展开，从方法、规模到现代替代技术，主旨是漂流瓶作为追踪洋流的工具。

questions.question: According to the passage, how were some drift bottles launched during the 1960s programme?
options: Some were released from aircraft flying along the Atlantic shelf.
They were all dropped by hand from research ships.
Satellites were used to position them at sea.
Local fishermen scattered them along the coastline.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段指出，在 1960 年代的项目中，研究者投放的超过七万个漂流瓶和海底漂流器中，有一些是从沿大西洋陆架飞行的飞机上投放的（some launched from aircraft sweeping along the Atlantic shelf）。

questions.question: How were scientists able to work out the direction and speed of a current from a bottle?
options: By tracking the bottle's exact route with radar the whole time.
By reading instruments built into each sealed bottle.
By asking ships to follow each bottle until it landed.
By comparing the bottle's release point with where it was recovered.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段说明，科学家通过比较投放地点与回收地点（comparing the release point with the recovery point）来推断洋流的方向和大致速度。

questions.question: What can we infer about why the drift bottle method has largely been abandoned?
options: Bottles were too expensive for governments to produce.
Newer tools give a more continuous and detailed picture of currents.
People are no longer willing to return any bottles they find.
Ocean currents have become too weak to move bottles.
questions.explanation_zh: 末段对比指出，漂流瓶只能告诉起点和终点而非完整路线，而 GPS 浮标能持续实时传回坐标，给出更详细的画面，可推断它被淘汰是因为新工具更连续、更精细。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "disperse" (in "disperse fish larvae") most nearly means
options: to count carefully.
to protect from harm.
to scatter or spread widely.
to gather into one place.
questions.explanation_zh: disperse fish larvae 指洋流把鱼苗向四处“散布、扩散”，所以最接近的意思是 scatter or spread widely（散开、广泛传播）。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把五个 Lesson 22 的通信与比较句式提升到 B2+ 更抽象的语境：never dreamed of ...ing 写意料之外的结果，of my own age 写同龄人之间的默契，never thought of it again 写被遗忘却日后回响的小举动，write to each other regularly 写跨国长期互通，will certainly ... faster 写更可靠方法的实际取舍。

patterns.title: never dreamed of ...ing
patterns.source: Jane never dreamed of receiving a letter from a girl of her own age in Holland.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 never dreamed of 加动名词，写某人完全没想到会发生的惊喜。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一项看似平凡的小举动，最终带来你当初完全没想到的深远结果或机遇。
patterns.sample: The researchers never dreamed of mapping an entire current system simply by releasing thousands of numbered bottles into the sea.
patterns.tip_zh: of 后面要接动名词形式，比如 receiving、meeting、finding。

patterns.title: of one's own age
patterns.source: a girl of her own age
patterns.focus_zh: 这个短语用来说明“和某人差不多大”，比只说 same age 更有课文味道。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你为什么更愿意把复杂的想法或担忧向一个同龄人倾诉，而不是向长辈。
patterns.sample: I find it far easier to confide my anxieties in a friend of my own age than in any teacher.
patterns.tip_zh: 写别人时可以换成 of his own age 或 of her own age；写自己时用 of my own age。

patterns.title: never thought of it again
patterns.source: She never thought of it again.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句子适合写一个小动作做完就忘了，后来却带来结果。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人随手完成一件不起眼的小事后便彻底抛诸脑后，直到多年后它意外地重新浮现。
patterns.sample: She quietly slipped the labelled card into the bottle, sealed it, and honestly never thought of it again for years.
patterns.tip_zh: it 要指代前面提到的那件小事；这样故事才有“后来突然回来”的感觉。

patterns.title: write to each other regularly
patterns.source: They write to each other regularly now.
patterns.focus_zh: write to each other 表示双方互相写；regularly 表示稳定、反复地做。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写两位身处不同国家的研究者或朋友，如何通过定期互通信息来维系一段长久的合作或友谊。
patterns.sample: Despite living on opposite sides of the ocean, the two scientists write to each other regularly to exchange their latest findings.
patterns.tip_zh: each other 不能只写单向动作；句子里要看得出两个人都在回应。

patterns.title: will certainly ... faster
patterns.source: Letters will cost a little more, but they will certainly travel faster.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式用来做实际比较：前半句承认成本，后半句强调更快、更可靠。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一种更可靠的方法虽然要多付出一些成本或精力，但几乎肯定会带来更快、更精确的结果。
patterns.sample: Deploying satellite-tracked buoys will certainly cost a little more, but the data will arrive far more reliably and faster.
patterns.tip_zh: but 后面要给出实际好处；faster 前面可以搭配 arrive、travel、work 等动词。
